sections.h2: Why do Coral Springs owners look at more than one way to sell?
sections.html:
Coral Springs sellers usually weigh a full listing against a quicker as-is sale, and the choice often turns on repairs, timing and a mortgage balance. The city describes itself as 24 square miles in the northwest corner of Broward County, with a family atmosphere and what it calls top-rated schools.

That family profile shows in the numbers: Census counts 3.01 persons per household, and 25.8 percent of residents are under 18. A household of that size usually needs a house with several bedrooms, which shapes who shops for a home here.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about housing in Coral Springs?
sections.html:
Coral Springs had 138,783 residents in the July 1, 2025 estimate, up 3.3 percent from the 2020 base, and its 22.86 square miles of land hold about 5,878 people per square mile. Owners occupy 60.3 percent of housing units.

sections.h2: How does the Broward County Property Appraiser affect a Coral Springs sale?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser sets values for Coral Springs addresses but does not send bills. Its home page states that a change in ownership resets the assessed value to full market value, so a buyer's taxes may be higher than yours.

  • Homestead filing for 2027 runs from March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027 for owners who made the home their permanent residence after January 1, 2026.
  • The last day to file late for any 2027 exemption is September 20, 2027, with no good-cause extension.
  • An Owner Alert service warns you if a document changing ownership of your property reaches the appraiser.

The Broward County Tax Collector sends the bills. Florida's early-payment discounts step down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1.

sections.h2: What taxes and recording costs come with a Coral Springs deed?
sections.html:
Outside Miami-Dade, the Department of Revenue says documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration or portion thereof, and s. 201.02 counts a mortgage or encumbrance on the property as consideration, whether or not it is assumed. Coral Springs falls under that standard rate because it is in Broward County.

  • The clerk collects the tax at recording.
  • Each party named on the deed is jointly liable, whichever side agrees to pay.
  • Clerk recording charges start at $5.00 for page one.

Ask your closing agent for a line-by-line statement.

sections.h2: What if you owe more than you can pay in Coral Springs?
sections.html:
Foreclosure in Florida ends with a court-ordered sale at least 20 and not more than 35 days after judgment, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer. A buyer deposits 5 percent of the bid, and with no objection within 10 days the sale is confirmed.

  • Surplus funds belong in a claim filed with the clerk before they are reported as unclaimed.
  • Homestead owners are told to check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure is a taxable deed for doc stamp purposes.

Selling before the judgment date can keep the proceeds in your hands.

sections.h2: How do inherited or rented Coral Springs houses differ?
sections.html:
An inherited house may need probate before it can be sold. Summary administration is open when non-exempt assets are $150,000 or less, or when the owner has been dead more than two years, under s. 735.201.

A landlord selling an occupied rental must handle the tenant lawfully. Month-to-month tenancies end with at least 30 days' notice, and a nonpayment notice allows 3 days, not counting weekends or court holidays. After a landlord wins in court the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before putting the landlord in possession. Coral Springs also has a large renter share, with 39.7 percent of housing units rented.

sections.h2: What should you do before accepting any Coral Springs offer?
sections.html:
1. Pull your payoff letter and check for liens.
  2. Confirm whether you filed for homestead, because ending it changes your January 1 assessment and your tax bill.
  3. Decide who covers the November tax bill.
  4. Make sure the deed will carry two witness signatures.

The Broward Property Appraiser answers recording and ownership questions through its FAQ page, and its phone line is 954-357-6830.

sections.h2: How do Save Our Homes and portability matter to a Coral Springs seller?
sections.html:
A long-time homestead owner in Coral Springs often holds an assessed value well under market value, because Save Our Homes caps yearly increases at the lower of 3 percent or the change in CPI. The Department of Revenue chart lists a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024.

A sale ends that cap on the old house. You can take part of the benefit to a new Florida home if the new homestead is established within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one. File Form DR-501T alongside the DR-501 by March 1. The statute lets the new assessed value drop by the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between the old house's just and assessed values; the amendments in chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 roll, so ask the appraiser how they affect you.

sections.h2: What relief exists for older owners and veterans in Coral Springs?
sections.html:
Several Florida programs reduce what an owner pays while living in the house, and each ends or changes at sale.

  • Owners 65 or older may qualify for an added exemption of up to $50,000 if the city or county adopted the ordinance and household income is within the limit; ask the Broward appraiser whether it applies.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember may receive a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • A homestead tax deferral through Form DR-570, filed with the tax collector by March 31, covers taxes above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

Deferred taxes accrue against the property, so they matter when you sell. Ask the Broward County Tax Collector for a payoff figure before closing.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Coral Springs?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists $545,400 as the median value of owner-occupied housing units in Coral Springs for 2020-2024.

faqs.q: Which county collects Coral Springs property taxes?
faqs.a: Broward County. The Property Appraiser sets values and the Broward County Tax Collector sends bills and takes payment.

faqs.q: What documentary stamp rate applies to a Coral Springs deed?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue prints 70 cents per $100 for every Florida county except Miami-Dade, so Broward's Coral Springs uses that rate.

faqs.q: When must I file for homestead?
faqs.a: By March 1 of the tax year, with the county property appraiser, and you must have made the home your permanent residence by January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell if the house is in probate?
faqs.a: Only after the personal representative has authority to convey, and a personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable for doc stamps.
